newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia interest rates seen staying firm -MIER.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia interest rates seen staying firm -MIER.

text.p: Malaysian interest rates are seen staying firm for the rest of this year and in the first half of 1997, a government-backed think-tank said on Tuesday.

The Malaysian Institute of Economic Research (MIER) said in a report that "interest rates are expected to remain firm for the rest of this year and even into the first two quarters of 1997 at least, as authorities will keep monetary policy tight".

MIER said the firm interest rates are needed "to contain inflationary pressure as loans growth is still very strong and the growth rate of money supply, though moderating, is still above levels consistent with price stability".
It forecast the three-month interbank offered rate (Klibor) at 7.2-7.4 percent in the first quarter of 1997.
In Tuesday morning trading, the three-month rate was quoted at 7.35/7.40 percent.
MIER said against the U.S. dollar and the yen, the ringgit appreciated by 1.7 percent and 7.9 percent respectively, between January and November this year.
But the ringgit's value against the Singapore dollar and the German mark remained almost unchanged during the same period.
"Sentiments on the ringgit are anticipated to remain favourable in the first quarter of 1997" due to high Malaysian interest rates, the think-tank said.
"However, seasonal demand for the greenback and the yen is expected to see the ringgit's exchange rate at 2.51-2.54 per dollar in the first quarter of 1997," the report said.
